- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show upward drift with no mean reversion, while true prices exhibit strong mean reversion after peaks.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+), model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, suggesting lag or failure to capture recent downward momentum.
- Forecasts are too smooth; fail to capture volatility or sudden drops in true prices.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher values, especially when recent history includes high prices (e.g., 80+), suggesting overconfidence in upward trend.
- Correction should reduce forecast slope after spikes and introduce downward adjustment in final 5–10 days.
- Use recent low prices (last 5–7 days) as a floor for forecast adjustment, especially if true price has recently declined.
